task_brief: Day 7 of "Professional Practice, Rights, and Pathways" (unit 2, grade 12) is an investigation on professional practice, rights, and pathways. It is one step inside the unit — not the whole unit project — and takes about 45–75 minutes. The unit is working toward: Assemble professional practice materials with a rights and licensing plan and a pathway action plan, timed to real application and audition deadlines. Today's work contributes to that by handling professional practice, rights, and pathways at the investigation or close reading stage, against the unit's wider topics of copyright licensing and contracts, pricing commissions and compensation, portfolio and application materials, and auditions interviews and submissions. This session produces reviewable evidence toward the unit performance task.
primary_task: Closely examine a work you did not make that demonstrates professional practice, rights, and pathways. Describe before you judge: what is present, how it is organised, and what happens over time or across the surface. Then interpret — what effect is created, and which specific element creates it. Support every claim with something a reader could check in the work itself. Finish with one question the work raises that you cannot answer from it alone. Use only public-domain, openly licensed, or properly cited works, and quote or excerpt no more than you need to make the point. Use the attached Academy-original reference work as the work under investigation; no outside artwork, recording, performance, or web source is required. Anchor today's work inside its unit: this session's evidence is about professional practice, rights, and pathways, and it belongs to "Professional Practice, Rights, and Pathways", which also covers separate topics such as copyright licensing and contracts. Close out with this check before you stop: State your interpretation of professional practice, rights, and pathways and the specific evidence that would change it. At grade 12 the bar is portfolio-quality independent work you could defend to an outside reader: intent stated, method justified, limitations named honestly, and revision traceable.

sourceReference:
ATTACHED MANUEL ACADEMY LEARNER RESOURCE

Resource ID: ma-resource:ma-g12-arts-and-music-u02-l07

Lesson focus: professional practice, rights, and pathways

Resource type: ACADEMY_ORIGINAL_REFERENCE_WORK

REFERENCE WORK — Mini-portfolio "Routes." Item A: three pencil thumbnails testing path direction. Item B: a four-event notated sound pattern testing repetition. Item C: a one-page reflection comparing which revision clarified intent. Sequence rationale: question → experiment → evidence. Rights log: every item is an Academy-original example. Access note: each item has a text description and may be reviewed privately. Use it to study professional practice, rights, and pathways; describe evidence before judging and adapt the example rather than copying a finished work.

How to use it: Use the attached Academy-original reference work as the work under investigation; no outside artwork, recording, performance, or web source is required.

Rights: Manuel Academy original; licensed CC BY 4.0 for learner use and adaptation. No third-party text, image, score, lyric, melody, recording, or performance is included.

Access and materials: Household-accessible route: pencil or pen and scrap paper are enough. For sound or performance work, tap, clap, use spoken syllables, move a finger, or notate silently. Specialized art materials, instruments, paid software, cameras, microphones, and recording devices are optional and never affect credit.
critique_criteria: Description precedes judgement, covering what is present and how it is organised.
Every interpretive claim points to something checkable in the work itself.
The specific element creating the effect is identified rather than the effect only named.
One unanswerable question raised by the work is stated.
Sources are public domain, openly licensed, or properly cited, and excerpts are no longer than the point requires.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available and scores the same. Instead of performing, speaking, or recording, you may submit a written description of what you made or would make, a notated or diagrammed version, a labelled plan, or a written analysis covering the same criteria. Nothing in this task requires a working microphone, camera, or the ability to perform aloud.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
For any multi-session project, supply a written milestone plan, checkpoint dates, and a task breakdown, so executive-function load is not silently part of what is being assessed.

Adjust quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode while holding the target constant. Where the target names a specific skill, change how it is evidenced rather than substituting a different skill.

Accept typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, notated, constructed, or demonstrated responses. Where performance is the target, a private demonstration to one trusted adult carries the same weight as any audience, and requires no recording.
Provide adaptive instruments and grips, enlarged or braille notation, seated and standing studio access, low-odour and low-dust material substitutes, and hearing protection on request.

Where documentation quality is itself the target, document the artwork alone with no person in frame, or have an adult verify the physical work directly. Neither route requires an image of the learner, and both preserve the documentation target rather than replacing it.
task_accessibility_provisions: Any model, source, or artifact under study is supplied in an accessible parallel form: text alternative or transcript, described version, and a tactile or enlarged rendering where the original is visual. The learner is never required to perceive the source in one specific channel to analyse it.
Breaks, extended time, a hidden timer, reduced copying, and a low-distraction setting are available on request and never reduce the score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, cultural context, and respectful representation.
Public performance is never required. A private, low-audience, or written-and-scored alternative always carries the same academic target.
No recording of the learner’s voice, no photograph, and no video is ever required; documentation may be written, notated, sketched, or adult-verified instead.
Use only original, public-domain, licensed, or family-approved works. Do not reproduce full copyrighted lyrics, sheet music, or other protected works without documented rights.
The tutor may explain technique, ask diagnostic questions, and critique work, but never silently completes graded creative work.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, score excerpt, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting professional practice, rights, and pathways.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile or concrete model, or adult demonstration.

remediation: Reteaching for professional practice, rights, and pathways follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for professional practice, rights, and pathways, model it in a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the approach to professional practice, rights, and pathways works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of professional practice, rights, and pathways, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "requests the answer to graded work": Explain the concept, ask a diagnostic question, or help isolate the defect. Do not supply the graded artifact, solution code, or finished creative work. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking professional practice, rights, and pathways mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension: Apply professional practice, rights, and pathways under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or explain the idea to someone else using an original example. Treat this as optional depth on professional practice, rights, and pathways rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
